newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures finished stronger but off their highs in moderate volume on Thursday after Russian President Boris Yeltsin fired Alexander Lebed, his security chief.
PIBOR futures and the franc benefitted from the news, as German assets weakened. The dollar traded sharply higher, which also lifted the franc, analysts said.
The news from Russia overshadowed the market's lack of reaction to a public sector strike in France. The strike was widely followed by teachers, train workers and other public sector workers.

Earlier, the notionnel had risen on market-friendly economic data from the United States. U.S. industrial production rose only slightly and capacity utilisation was lower in September, weekly jobless claims rose and the Philadelphia Federal Reserve business survey was weaker, all lifting bond markets in Europe.
Traders also reported that U.S. funds covered shorts in PIBOR and sold marks for francs in early afternoon.

Traders said that aside from the news of Lebed's dismissal, the franc was supported by foreign buying on relief Thursday's strike did not paralyse the economy. U.S. funds are also reportedly targetting franc resistance at 3.3750/60 per mark.
